memos.scout:
The case for buying is thin but not zero. In the first two minutes after graduation, 279 buyers put in 318 SOL, and the top five buyers held only 23% of that flow, which argues against a single operator dominating the launch. The last 15 minutes show 396 buyers against 306 sellers and 305 SOL bought versus 265 sold, a net inflow of about 40 SOL and a 1.18x return over that window. The coin is alive, its 30-minute return is up 74%, and pool depth of 104 SOL is deep enough that a $20 ticket won't move the price much.

Against that, the coin has already fallen 44% from its 30-minute high, the sell-to-buy ratio at launch was 0.92, and a launch bot was present. The curve data (bundle share, completer share, top-3 share) is missing, so the bundling and concentration picture is unknown. Name and symbol are null, and the classification is UNRESOLVED. With the drawdown, the unknown curve structure, and the base rates against random buys, I can't make a strong honest case that demand will hold for the next 30-60 minutes. The honest call is to skip, or at most treat this as a low-conviction speculative entry.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is a late-stage distribution after the dip. The coin is down 44% from its 30-minute high, yet still shows a +74% 30-minute return, so early buyers are up big and sellers are active: last 15 minutes show 265 SOL sold against 305 SOL bought (sell/buy ~0.87), 306 sellers vs 396 buyers, and net flow of only +40 SOL. A launch bot was present and the first two minutes had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.92, consistent with snipers exiting into new buyers. The curve data is entirely null (bundle share, top-3 holders, completer share), so insider concentration can't be ruled out. The pool is thin at 104 SOL, so a $20 round trip would lose roughly 2-5% to impact and fees, and any further distribution would hit that shallow depth quickly. With the coin's class unresolved and the base rate for random post-graduation buys around -20%, the skeptical call is to pass.
